History
Here at Round Hill, you are in touch with over 200 years of
Pennsylvania history. After this land was purchased by the
Peairs family in 1790, seven generations of the family lived
here. Imagine living on the same land as your great, great,
great, great grandparents. In fact, one of the earliest farmers
here was a soldier in the American Revolution. Imagine
what it would be like to plow the fields without tractors,
give water to the animals without indoor plumbing, and
store your food without refrigeration or electricity.

Animals at Round Hill Farm
Sheep
Shearing sheep is like giving them a haircut. During the cold
months their wool helps keep them warm. They are sheared in
the spring before the warmer summer months. The wool can
be made into yarn or fabric for clothes, blankets and rugs.
How many sweaters do you think can be made from the wool
of one sheep? The wool right off the sheep may weigh from 2
to 10 lbs. After cleaning, combing and spinning the wool,
there is usually enough product for about 2-3 sweaters. What
time of year are you visiting? How fluffy are the
sheep? When do you think they were last sheared?
Cattle
The cows at Round Hill are Brown Swiss, one of the two most
popular dairy cow breeds in the world. They can be milked
twice a day, and each cow can produce more than 5 gallons
of milk per day. Cheese, yogurt, ice cream; what is
your favorite milk product?
Rabbits
A female rabbit, (a doe) can have a lot of babies (kits). It only
takes about 30 days for a doe to give birth to a litter of 4-8
kits. A doe can have around 70 kits a year. See how the
rabbits have different appearances? The poster on
the wall shows over 50 breeds of rabbits. Can you
identify any of the breeds here?
Turkeys
Did you know that turkeys lay eggs that humans can eat, but
we donʼt often see them at the store? Compared to chickens, it

raise turkeys for meat, not eggs. Is there a certain time of
year you might eat turkey?

Pigs
Have you ever heard “your room looks like a pigsty”? These
pigs and their enclosure may look dirty, but itʼs for a good
reason. Pigs do not sweat enough to cool their bodies.
They roll in the mud to stay cool, protect them from the

sun, and add a layer of insect protection. Donʼt worry! Pigs
have different areas to go to the bathroom, to sleep, eat, and
roll. How do you stay cool in the summer?
Horses
After a career with the mounted Allegheny County Police, these
horses enjoy their retirement on Round Hill Farm. Because of their
age they receive a special softer diet. The horse
pasture is next to the cow pasture and provides an
opportunity for grazing and exercise. You can
visit their active co-workers on Corrigan
Drive in South Park.
Goats
Goats can have jobs! “Goat-scaping” is when a herd of goats
is brought into hard-to-maintain areas to graze on the
vegetation. Their climbing skills and appetite make them great
at clearing spaces like on hillsides or areas full of brambles.
Here at the farm, they still like to climb. What do you see in
their enclosure to give them a chance to climb?
Chickens
There are hundreds of breeds of chickens, and they lay a
variety of egg colors. White and brown are the most
recognized but there are shades of blues, greens, and pinks.
Did you know that chicken diet, age, and egg freshness all
influence the taste of an egg? Look at the breed poster in the
chicken house. Can you identify any of the breeds here
at the farm?
Donkeys
Youʼve heard of a guard dog, but what about a guard
donkey? Wild predators like coyotes can eat smaller farm
animals like goats, sheep, or chickens. Farmers use donkeys to
protect herds of animals, almost like a superhero. To defend
other animals, donkeys use their powerful kick and strong bite
to keep the herd safe. If you created a donkey
superhero, what name would you give it?
Alpacas
Is that an alpaca or a llama? Both alpacas and llamas
originated in South America. Alpacas have shorter faces and
snouts than llamas. Farmers use alpacas for their soft hair, or
fleece. The fleece can be used to make yarn, hats, and
clothes. What other animal on the farm has similar
hair?
